title: A new idempotency key on every click defeats the double-refund protection in exactly the ambiguous-failure case
evidence: api.js:32 says the key lets the server ignore a repeated request for the same attempt, and README line 8 says a repeated request must not refund twice. app.js:128 mints a fresh key per click. After a failure the catch at app.js:131-133 keeps state.selected, and the finally block re-enables the button. A network error (api.js:13), an invalid-JSON body (api.js:19) and a 5xx all land there, and the server may already have refunded. The guard against a retry is wording only. Traced.
failing_case: User refunds 3 orders. The server processes the refunds, but the response is lost or the proxy times out, so the user sees 'The refund was not confirmed. The server could not be reached.' The 3 rows are still ticked and 'Refund 3 orders' is enabled. The user clicks it again and confirms; the new UUID is a different key, so the server refunds the 3 orders a second time. The same happens if the refund endpoint answers 200/204 with an empty body: res.json() throws at api.js:17, a success is reported as a failure, and the retry pays twice.
remediation: Create the key once per selection attempt and keep it until the server gives a definitive answer, or until the selection changes. After an ambiguous failure, clear the selection and force a reload before another refund. Do not require a JSON body from the refund endpoint.

title: Every order is selectable and refundable whatever its status; the refund eligibility rule exists nowhere
evidence: app.js:34-45 renders a checkbox for every row, including status 'refunded', 'pending' and 'unknown'. refundSelected (app.js:119-123) takes whatever is selected and sums o.total for the confirmation. domain.js has no eligibility function. The README lists the server checks (README.md:7-10) as authorisation and idempotency only, not a status check.
failing_case: Filter to 'refunded', tick one $50.00 order and click 'Refund 1 order'. The dialog says 'Refund 1 order totalling $50.00? This sends money back to the customers.' and POSTs the id. The same happens for a 'pending' order that was never charged. The confirmation then states an amount that is not refundable, and the only barrier is a server rule nobody documented.

requirement.why: Refunding an already-refunded or unpaid order is not a sensible action; domain.js already treats non-paid orders as zero revenue (domain.js:26).

remediation: Add a pure isRefundable(order) in domain.js (status === 'paid') with a test. Disable the checkbox for other statuses and exclude them from the confirmation total. Document the matching server-side check.

title: Paging is not announced, and Next disables itself while it has focus
evidence: #page is a plain span (index.html:34), not a live region. Next/Previous call renderTable (app.js:145-146), which replaces every row and sets $('next').disabled at app.js:72. WCAG 4.1.3 (AA) needs the result of the action to be announced. README line 5 admits no screen-reader test. Traced; I did not drive a browser.
failing_case: A screen-reader user presses Next on page 1 of 2. Page 2's rows replace page 1's and nothing is spoken. Because the button is now disabled while focused, keyboard focus is lost to the document and the user must tab back from the top to find the table.
remediation: Give #page role='status' (or aria-live='polite'). When a pager button disables itself, move focus to the table caption or the other pager button.

title: normaliseOrder turns a missing total (null, empty string, empty array, true) into a valid 0 or 1 instead of dropping the record
evidence: The comment at domain.js:7 and the skipped-record message in app.js:103 promise that records with no numeric total are dropped and counted. Number(null) is 0, Number('') is 0, Number([]) is 0 and Number(true) is 1, and Number.isFinite accepts all of them, so the guard at domain.js:12 passes. Only undefined and non-numeric strings are caught. Traced; I could not execute it because Bash was denied mid-run.
failing_case: The API returns {id:'A7', total:null, status:'paid', customer:{name:'Dana'}}. The row shows $0.00, the 'could not be shown' note never appears, and the order can be ticked and sent to /refunds. With total:'' or total:[] the result is the same. A corrupted total looks like a real $0.00 order, and the stats count it.
remediation: Reject unless typeof raw.total is 'number' or a non-empty string, then convert and check Number.isFinite. Add a normaliseOrder test for null, '', [] and true.

title: Revenue adds 8.25% tax (and a gold discount) on top of the order total the table shows, so the stat does not reconcile with the rows
evidence: orderRevenueCents multiplies the server's order.total by 1.0825 (and by 0.9 for gold). The table (app.js:51) and the refund confirm (app.js:122) show and use the raw total. An order total from an API normally already includes tax and discount, and revenue normally excludes tax. Nothing in the repo states which it is. Traced.
failing_case: One paid standard order with total 100.00. The row says $100.00 and the Revenue card says $108.25. For a gold order the row says $100.00 and Revenue says $97.43. The user cannot reconcile the two, and the refund prompt for the same order says $100.00.

requirement.why: Inferred from the usual meaning of an order total and of revenue; no spec in the payload defines total as pre-tax or pre-discount.

remediation: Settle in one named domain function whether order.total is net or gross. Compute revenue, the average and the refund amount from that single function, and add tests with a gold order and a taxed order.

title: After a confirmed refund, a failed reload leaves the orders selected, stale and refundable again under a new idempotency key
evidence: app.js:128-130 calls refund(), shows the success toast, then awaits load(). load() never throws: it catches its own errors (app.js:105-108) and only clears state.selected and replaces state.orders inside the success branch (app.js:96-98). On a failed reload both stay as they were. renderRefundButton() then runs in the finally at app.js:136 with n > 0 and refunding false, so the button is enabled and reads 'Refund N orders'. Each click makes a new key (app.js:128), so the server cannot dedupe against the first request. Traced, not driven (no shell was available).
failing_case: Select 2 paid orders and click Refund, then confirm. POST /refunds succeeds and the toast says 'Refunded 2 orders.'. The follow-up GET /orders fails with a network blip or a 502. The table still shows both orders as 'paid' and both stay checked. The button still says 'Refund 2 orders'. The user sees the red 'Orders could not be loaded' message, clicks Refund and confirms again. A second POST goes out with a fresh Idempotency-Key and the customers are refunded twice, if the server does not also reject already-refunded orders. The README does not say that it does.
remediation: Clear state.selected, and mark or remove the refunded ids from state.orders, as soon as refund() resolves, before the reload. A failed reload then cannot leave the refunded rows selectable.
